instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. 2 tests in describe("lasso selection modes") still fail under `yarn test:app --watch=false`: (1) `respects arrow bound label enclosure and ignores container bound label in contain mode` -> AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1 at selection.test.tsx:1678 (`assertSelectedElements([arrow.id])` after the second drawLasso); (2) `enforces group containment across visible, off-screen, locked, and bound-text members and preserves frame/shift behaviour` -> AssertionError: expected undefined to be true at :1826 (`expect(h.state.selectedElementIds[groupContainer.id]).toBe(true)`). Cause, measured with a probe: the describe's beforeAll calls mockBoundingClientRect() with its defaults, which put the canvas at left: 20, top: 10, so h.state.offsetLeft = 20 and offsetTop = 10 and every mouse coordinate becomes scene coordinate (x - 20, y - 10). drawLasso([[-20,-10],[120,-10],[120,110],[-20,110]]) is the scene lasso [[-40,-20],[100,-20],[100,100],[-40,100]], whose right edge x=100 touches the arrow's end point (0..100), so contain mode correctly rejects the arrow; likewise [[-10,-10],[60,-10],[60,60],[-10,60]] becomes x -30..40, crossing groupContainer's right edge at x=40. The lasso code is correct (a probe without the offset selects the arrow, and selects G2 with its members). Fix in the tests only: call mockBoundingClientRect({ top: 0, left: 0, bottom: 0, right: 0, width: 1920, height: 1080, x: 0, y: 0, toJSON: () => {} }) in that beforeAll so screen and scene coordinates coincide (offsetLeft = offsetTop = 0), and then check every drawLasso in describe("lasso selection modes") against the scene coordinates of its elements: each lasso meant to enclose an element must clear its outline (and an arrow's label) by a margin of at least 10 on every side, and each meant to clip must actually cross it. Keep the expectations; change only the mock call and, where needed, lasso coordinates. No toMatchSnapshot() calls; no test outside this describe changes.

The file's current text is under Inputs, marked "current text"; your edits apply to exactly that text.

## Answer
Return ONLY a JSON object {"path": "packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx", "edits": [{"search": "<text copied exactly from the current text>", "replace": "<its replacement>"}]} with no other text. Each search must appear exactly once in the current text; the edits apply in order.
If the file does not exist yet, or the change rewrites most of it, return {"path": "packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx", "content": "<the complete file>"} instead.
